In the format pane, go to Layout, then Matrix layout, and choose Tabular to put each row field in its own column with no indentation. Compact is the indented layout, and Outline also gives each field its own column but shows subtotals at the top of each group.
Update, November 2026: Power BI now labels this dropdown Row level, where the text and screenshots say Series. It is under Row subtotals, Apply settings to, Per row level.

paragraphs: Update, November 2026: The screenshots in this post have been lost. The text still refers to them. The table of ranges and the measure are needed to follow the post, so they are given below in update notes.

Update, November 2026: The screenshot of this table is lost. A table with these three columns works with the measure below. The ranges here are an example, not the original's: Min Value is the lowest total in the range, and Max Value is where the next range starts. Set the last Max Value above any customer's total so that "and over" holds; 1,000,000,000 is used here.
Update, November 2026: Sort by Column is now on the Column tools tab, which appears when you select the Range Name column.

Update, November 2026: The original measure was a screenshot that has been lost. This version is rebuilt from Alison's reply to a reader in April 2021, which gave a percentage version of it; the percentage part is taken out here.

For each range, it counts the customers whose Total Sales are at least the Min Value and less than the Max Value. SUMX adds the ranges together, so the total row counts once each customer whose Total Sales falls inside one of the ranges. A customer with no sales in the year counts as zero, so they fall in a range that starts at 0.
notes.code:
No of Customers with these Total Sales =
SUMX (
    Bins,
    COUNTROWS (
        FILTER (
            Customers,
            [Total Sales] >= Bins[Min Value]
                && [Total Sales] < Bins[Max Value]
        )
    )
)

paragraphs: Update, November 2026: 8.4 is rounded down to 8, not up. The filter keeps every rank that is 8.4 or less, which is ranks 1 to 8.
Update, November 2026: The % button is now on the Column tools tab, in the Formatting group, when the Percent column is selected.
Update, November 2026: This measure has its two rank columns the wrong way round. The corrected measure is in the update note below it.

Update, November 2026: In this measure, Top_PC filters on the Customers Ranked Bottom column and Bottom_PC on Customers Ranked Top, so choosing Top returns the bottom customers and choosing Bottom returns the top ones. Swap the two columns, so that each matches the measures in Approach No. 1:
notes.code:
Top/Bottom Percent =
VAR Rank_To_Find = COUNTROWS ( ALL ( Customers ) ) * SELECTEDVALUE ( 'Percent'[Percent] )
VAR Top_or_Bottom = SELECTEDVALUE ( 'Top or Bottom'[Top or Bottom] )
VAR Top_PC =
    CALCULATE ( [_Total Sales],
        FILTER ( Customers, Customers[Customers Ranked Top] <= Rank_To_Find ) )
VAR Bottom_PC =
    CALCULATE ( [_Total Sales],
        FILTER ( Customers, Customers[Customers Ranked Bottom] <= Rank_To_Find ) )
RETURN
    IF ( Top_or_Bottom = "top", Top_PC, Bottom_PC )
